discovery_graph._comment: The real set of directories each agent scans for skills, verified against each agent's own docs/source (not guessed). `dedup_kind` is the load-bearing field for the one-skill-one-entry invariant: `by-path` means the agent turns every contributing path into its own catalog entry, so more than one contribution IS a user-visible duplicate; `by-name` means the agent merges the identity itself and shows exactly one entry, so several contributions are ordinary cross-agent reuse and never a defect. It must state what the agent really does, established from its source or from its own rendered catalog -- never assumed. `write_root` names a key in `targets` this repo actually writes to; null means the agent reads that path natively but this repo must NOT write there, because it is redundant with (or deprecated in favor of) a `write_root` this repo already populates. Adding a physical copy at a null-write_root path would create a real duplicate in that agent's effective catalog, not fix one. See `discovery_graph_notes.md` for the underlying evidence per agent.

roots.note: project-scoped root under the working directory; this repo ships one skill there. Do not write user-profile content here.

claude-code.dedup: single-root; no cross-tool overlap. Non-recursive, so a bundle's nested skills never enter this catalog at all

roots.note: deprecated by Codex itself, kept only for backward compatibility -- do not write here. Scanned recursively, so its dot-prefixed `.system/` subtree of Codex's own built-in skills is part of this root, not a separate one.

cache of plugin-provided skills (`<plugin>/<version>/skills/<name>`), which enter the catalog namespaced as `<plugin>:<skill>`. Only *installed and enabled* plugins actually reach the runtime, and install state is not derivable from the filesystem, so this root is expected to over-report -- see `install_gated` handling in audit_catalog.runtime_check(). Codex populates it; do not write here.

project-scoped root under the working directory, scanned in addition to the user roots. A repository that vendors a skill also installed globally therefore shows it twice -- this repo's own .agents/skills is exactly that shape, so the root has to be modelled, not assumed absent.

codex.dedup: by-path, not by name: a same-name skill present at two roots (or at two subdirectories within the SAME root) is shown twice, unmerged. Verified empirically against `codex debug prompt-input` -- see discovery_graph_notes.md

roots.note: external compat scan, on by default
external compat scan, on by default; scanned after .claude, wins ties
OpenCode's own root; redundant once .agents/skills is populated -- do not write here

opencode.dedup: by name, last-scan-wins, logs a warning on collision. The agent merges the identity itself, so several contributing paths surface as exactly one catalog entry

cursor.dedup: by name: Cursor documents no rule, so this was verified empirically in Cursor's Skills UI (2026-09-10) with the shared roots below populated -- every identity appeared exactly once, including ones reachable from three roots at the same time

duplicate_exceptions_comment: The ONLY sanctioned way one logical skill identity may appear more than once in a single agent's discovery graph. Each entry is an object: {"agent": <key in discovery_graph>, "logical_id": <the namespaced identity the runtime shows>, "paths": [<every contributing path, home-relative, forward slashes>], "reason": <why both are wanted>, "reviewed": <YYYY-MM-DD>}. `paths` must match the real contributing set EXACTLY -- differ by one path and the exception does not apply, so an exception can never silently widen to cover a duplicate nobody reviewed. An exception matching no current duplicate is itself a PROBLEM. Empty is the correct steady state.
